SECTIONA.NATIONALPLAN
1.OVERVIEWANDPROCESSFORESTABLISHINGTHEPLAN
1.1.Executivesummary
i.Political,economic,environmentalandsocialcontextoftheplan
NECP is a strategic document aimed at harmonizing energy and climate policies to ensuresustainabledevelopmentandrecoveryofUkraine'seconomy.
The preparationof NECPis anobligationof Ukraine withintheframeworkoftheTreatyontheEstablishment of the EnergyCommunity
1
inaccordancewiththerequirementsoftheRegulation(EU) 2018/1999 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018ontheGovernance of the Energy Union and Climate Action, , amending Regulations (EC) No663/2009 and (EC) No 715/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council, Directives94/22/EC, 98/70/EC, 2009/31/EC, 2009/73/EC, 2010/31/EU, 2012/27/EUand 2013/30/EUofthe European Parliament and of the Council, Council Directives 2009/119/EC and (EU)2015/652 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 525/2013 of the European Parliament andof theCouncil (hereinafter -Regulation(EU)2018/1999)andtheCommissionNotice
2
.TheNECPwasdevelopedtoimplement the Decrees of thePresidentofUkraineofNovember8,2019,No.837
3
and of March 23, 2021 No. 111
4
. Inaddition, the development andapproval of the NECPis acondition for the distribution of EUfinancial assistance within the framework of the UkraineFacility.
The NECP was prepared in accordance with the clear requirements of the Regulation (EU)2018/1999
5
, as well as takingintoaccounttheexperienceofpreparingsimilardocumentsbytheEU member states and the Contracting Parties of the Energy Community and previousdevelopments
6
. The development of the draft NECP was carried out by a group of leadingexperts of DiXi Group think tank and the State Institution "Institute for Economics andForecasting of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine" with the support of the UKEmbassy (the project "Ukrainian national development andpreparationfor the implementationoftheenergyandclimateplan")andtheU.S.initiativeNetZeroWorld.
On the part of the Government of Ukraine, the Ministry of Economy coordinates thedevelopment of the NECP. The Resolutionof the CabinetofMinistersofUkraineofAugust19,2023, No. 924 (Official Gazette of Ukraine, 2023, No. 84, Article 4855) established anInteragency Working Group on Preparation of Proposals and Recommendations for theDevelopment of the National EnergyandClimatePlan
7
,towhichareattachedallkeyministriesanddepartments.

At the same time, the full-scale invasion of the RussianFederationintoUkraine has a seriousimpact on the Ukrainian economy, in particular the energy sector. One of the most importantaspects is the destructionofcriticalinfrastructurefacilitiesasaresultofhostilities,whichcausessignificant interruptions inthe supplyof electricityandgas, as well as disrupts theoperationofdistrict heating systems. Thus, only in the period fromNovember 2022 to February 2023, onaverage, electricity supply was limitedto3.8millionconsumers, andthe maximumnumber ofconsumers cut off due toshellingduringa systemaccident inthe UESofUkrainereached13.5million
8
. Further attacks oncritical infrastructure facilitiesmayexacerbatetheenergycrisisandlimit access to key resources. In addition, hostilities affect the supply of labor and businessactivities.
In general, fromthe beginning of the full-scale aggression until the endof the autumn-winterperiod of 2022/2023, about 50%of available generatingcapacities andtransformer substationsof the transmission system of Ukrenergo were temporarily lost (damaged and occupied).According to the assessment of the Kyiv School of Economics (KSE) in accordance withthemethodology of the World Bank, as of May 2024, as a result of the full-scale invasionof theRussian Federation on the territory of Ukraine, the energy sector suffered direct losses andindirect financial losses inthe amount of 56.5billionUSD, while theneedsforrecovery,whichprovide for the complete reconstruction of destroyedfacilities under the principle "BuildBackBetter" amountedto50.5billionUSD. More than18GWof generatingcapacitywasoccupied,the Kakhovska and Dniprovska HPPs, the Zmiivska and Trypilska TPPs were completelydestroyed, andotherTPPssufferedcriticaldamage.Abouthalfofthehigh-voltagesubstationsofthe electricitytransmissionsystemwere damaged, all oil refineries anda significant part of theinfrastructure for the storage of crude oil andpetroleumproductswereactuallydestroyed
9
.Asaresult of the full-scale invasionof the RussianFederationintoUkrainefromFebruary2022,theconsumption of natural gas (-28.7%in 2022 compared to 2021) and electricity (-30-35%), aswellastheproductionofnaturalgas(-6.7%in2022comparedto2021)havedecreased.
Withthe beginningof thefull-scaleinvasionoftheRussianFederationintoUkraine,thenumberof cyberattacks increased dramatically - in the first 47 days alone, 200,000 events related tocyber security
10
were recorded, andfromJanuary2022toSeptember 2023, CERT-UArecordedalmost4,000cyberincidents
11
.Mostcyberattacksoccurintheelectricitysector.Forexample,thehacker group Sandworm, associated with the special services of the Russian Federation, bycyberattacks onOctober 10and12, 2022, increasedthe effect of massive missileattacksontheenergysystemofUkraine
12
.
As of the beginning of 2024, the estimated damage caused to the environment exceeded 56billion EUR, with more than 3,300 documented legal cases
13
. The prosecutor's office wasinvestigating280criminalcasesofecocideandenvironmentalwarcrimes.Thus,themainproblemsofthedevelopmentandimplementationofNECPare:
● Continuationof hostilities andthe needtotake intoaccounttheirconsequences,uncertaintyabout the scale of the destruction and the pace of recovery, which directly affects thepossibility of implementing certain defined policies and measures, the pace of theirimplementationandsuccess;

ii.StrategyrelatingtothefivedimensionsoftheEnergyUnion
Ukraine has a developed systemof legislation and regulation, as well as a fairly wide set ofpolicies andmeasures inthefieldsofenergy,climateandrelatedareas.Bothatthenationalleveland at the regional level (within the Energy Community), Ukraine has defined key goals by2030,inparticular:
● Reductionofgreenhousegasemissionsby65%ascomparedtothe1990level;
● Theshareofrenewableenergysourcesintotalfinalenergyconsumptionisatleast27%;
● Primaryenergyconsumptionisnomorethan72.224Mtoe,finalenergyconsumption-than42.168Mtoe;
● Theforecastedenergysavingsinthebuildingsofstateauthoritiesisnotlessthan21.4toeperyear;
● Reductionofthelevelofimportdependence(grossimportsinthetotalprimaryenergysupply)to33%;
● Deepeningthediversificationofsourcesandroutesofenergysupply-nomorethan30%fromasinglesupplier;
● CompleteandcomprehensiveintegrationoftheelectricityandnaturalgasmarketsofUkrainewiththeEuropeanmarket;
● Freepricingonenergymarketswithmechanismstosupportvulnerableconsumers;
● Developmentandfinancingofinnovationandresearchinthesectorofcleantechnologies,renewableenergyandlow-carbonproduction;
● Increasingcompetitiveness;
● Climateneutralityoftheenergysectorby2050.
At the same time, issues of completeness (sufficiency), relevance andharmonizationofpoliciesand measures aimed at achieving the main strategic goals come to the foreground, especiallygiven the need to build a full-fledged climate governance architecture taking intoaccount thestandards of sustainable corporate governance. Actually, the NECP is aimed at harmonizingenergy and climate policies, filling gaps and adjusting the content of individual measures toachievethedefinedgoals.
A detailed overview of key energy and climate policies and measures related to the fivedimensions of the Energy Union is presented in section 1.2.ii. The development of modelingscenarios in accordance with the requirements of the Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 took placetaking into account the peculiarities of public administration in Ukraine (see Appendix 1 fordetails).

1.2.Overviewofcurrentpolicysituation
i.NationalandEnergyCommunityenergysystemandpolicycontextofthenationalplan
As a ContractingPartyof the EnergyCommunity,aswellaswithintheprocessofaccessiontotheEU,Ukraine undertookthe commitment todevelopNECPinaccordance withRegulation(EC) 2018/1999andthenotificationoftheEuropeanCommission.
Since 2016, Ukraine has beenworkingonthe implementationof the AssociationAgreement betweenUkraine and the EU, including the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area. According to theassessment oftheCabinetofMinistersofUkraine
14,
asof2023,77%oftheobligationsstipulatedbytheAgreement have been fulfilled, in particular: in the field of energy - 78%, environment and civilprotection-80%,energyefficiency,housingandutilities-78%.
OnFebruary28, 2022, Ukraine officiallyappliedformembershipintheEuropeanUnion.OnMarch1,2022, the European Parliament adopted a resolution supporting granting Ukraine the status of acandidate for EUmembership, and on March 10-11, 2022, at the informal summit of the EuropeanCouncil in Versailles, EU leaders recognized the European prospects and the European choice ofUkraine, as specified in the Association Agreement andsupportedthe decisionof the EUCouncil toinvite the Commission to provide its opiniononthis applicationinaccordance withthe provisions ofthe relevant treaties. On April 17, 2022, Ukraine submitted answers to the European Commission'sQuestionnaire onUkraine's compliancewiththepoliticalandeconomiccriteriaforEUmembership,onMay 9 - the second part of the Questionnaire onthe compliance of Ukrainianlegislation, institutionsand practice with EU law in 33 areas. The EU decision to grant Ukraine the official status of acandidatecountrywasadoptedonJune23,2022.

Decarbonization(developmentofrenewableenergysources)
The maindocuments establishingthe legislative frameworkfor renewable energysourcesarethelawsof Ukraine "On Alternative EnergySources"
32
and"OnAlternative Fuels"
33
. These laws transposedpart of the provisions of Directive (EU) 2018/2001of December 11, 2018onthepromotionoftheuseofenergyfromrenewablesourcesintoUkrainianlegislation.
Since 2009, the development of renewable energysources inthe electricitysector has beendue totheintroductionof a fixed"green" tariff (feed-intariff) model. Thus, asofthebeginningof2022,thetotalvolume of installedcapacityofrenewableenergyfacilitiesfor"green"tariffamountedtomorethan9.5GW(10.1 GWtaking into account facilities occupied until February 24, 2022), and the volume ofinvestmentsintheindustryexceeded12billionUSdollars.
At the same time, thesupportsystembasedonthe"green"tariffmodel,duetothelackoffeedbackandmarket pricing mechanisms, did not form a sustainable approach to the development of renewableenergyinUkraine.Therapid,morethantripledgrowthofelectricityproductionfromalternativeenergysources during2019-2021has createda number of economic andtechnical challenges associatedwithboth the lack of a sustainable financial systemof payment for electricity produced fromrenewablesources and limited opportunities of the unified energy system of Ukraine to the integration ofrenewableenergyfacilities.
In October 2019, the Government started public discussions with all interested parties in order toresolve problematic issues in the field of renewable energy. The process involved the DisputeResolution and Negotiation Center of the EnergyCommunitySecretariat as a mediator, as a result ofwhich compromise agreements were reached, outlined in the Memorandumonmutual understandingregardingthesettlementofproblematicissuesinthefieldofrenewableenergyinUkraine.

The key ones are: on the part of investors - voluntary agreement to reduce "green" tariffs, increaseresponsibilityfor imbalances, limit the terms of puttingsolar power plants intooperationaccordingtothe "green" tariff model; on the part of the state - ensuring stable current payment for the generatedelectricity, repayment of accumulateddebt andpromotionof further development of the industryonacompetitivebasis.
Given the difficult situation in the industry, Ukraine did not go for a unilateral reductionof "green"tariffs, but reached a settlement of this issue through long negotiations with investors, search forcompromises and conclusion of the Memorandum, which became the basis of the relevant lawofUkraine.
Since that time,Ukrainehasensuredrepaymentofdebttoinvestorsinrenewablegeneration.Currently,the relevant problematic issues are related to the challenges facing the energysystem, inconnectionwiththefull-scaleinvasionoftheRussianFederationintoUkraine.
At the endof 2021, as part of the Treatyonthe Establishment of the EnergyCommunity(decisionofthe Council of Ministers of the Energy Community of November 30, 2021 No. 2021/14/МС-ЕпС),Ukraine undertook the commitment to implement the fourth energy package "Clean Energy forEuropeans", whichincludes Directive (EC)2018/2001ofDecember11,2018"Onthepromotionoftheuseofenergyfromrenewablesources"(REDII).
InOctober 2023, the EUapprovedEUDirective 2023/2413, whichupdatedthe provisions of REDII,and since then the Directive has received the name RED III, which, in particular, provides for anincrease in the share of energyfromRES. Inthe case of Ukraine's accessiontothe EU, Ukraine willpotentially also have to implement the provisions of the RED III Directive and the correspondingdelegated regulations, which are stricter than the current requirements for the Energy Communitymember states. Currently, the Government is working on the development of a draft law on thecomprehensive implementation of the requirements of European legislation inthe fieldof renewableenergydevelopment.
The National Economic Strategy of Ukraine for the perioduntil 2030, approvedbythe Resolutionofthe Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine of March3, 2021No. 179(Official Gazette of Ukraine, 2021p.,No. 22, Article 1015) (hereinafter - NES), defines one of the keyguidelines intheeconomicpolicyofUkraine, the decarbonizationof the economy(increasingenergyefficiency, developmentofrenewableenergy sources, development of circular economy and synchronization with the "European GreenCourse"initiative).
Further, the order of theCabinetofMinistersofUkraineofApril21,2023No.373(OfficialGazetteofUkraine, 2023 p., No. 47, Article 2575) approvedthe EnergyStrategyof Ukraine for the perioduntil2050 (hereinafter - ESU)
34
, which, in particular, determines the indicative indicators of the futuredevelopment of renewable energy. Among them: achieving a share of 27%of energyproducedfromrenewable energy sources in total final energyconsumptionby2030, 70%of energyfromrenewablesources intotal primaryenergysupplyby2050andreachingclimateneutralityoftheenergysectorby2050.
The use of renewable energy sources is one of the most important areas of Ukraine's energy policyaimed at saving traditional fuel and energy resources, improving the state of the environment, andpreventingclimate change. Increasingthe share of renewable sources inUkraine's energybalancewillcontribute to the decarbonization process of the economy, necessary for the fulfillment of Ukraine'sinternational obligations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and to reduce the consequences of theintroductionoftheCarbonBorderAdjustmentMechanism(CBAM)bytheEuropeanUnion.
Increasing the share of energy carriers obtained fromrenewable sources will contribute to ensuringenergysecurityandachievingenergyindependenceofthestatebydiversifyingenergysources.
Policies andmeasures under the dimension"decarbonization" are presentedindetail insection3.1.ofthisPlan.

2.4.3.MarketintegrationThe priority direction of the EU energy policy, fixed in the REPowerEU plan, foresees severalcomponents that significantly affected the value of gas as an energy resource for the transition to acarbon-neutral economy in 2050. Many EU member states, in particular those that have their ownnatural gas production and/or are significantlydependent ongas, intheir NECPs directlyindicate thekey role of gas in meeting energy needs in the mediumterm. This recognition is accompaniedbyanumberofpoliciesandmeasuresrelatedtonaturalgasandoil,namely:● increaseofownproduction,includingdevelopmentofcontinentalshelfresources(Romania,Italy);● newconstruction, modernizationandoptimizationof infrastructure toincreasecross-borderflows,includingstrengtheningthecapacityofsystemswithinthecountry(Romania,Italy,Bulgaria).

As a result, in 2030 they predict a significant share of natural gas in meeting energy needs (forexample,inItaly-33-38%from41%in2021).At the same time, other countries set a date for the endof hydrocarbonexplorationanddevelopment:forexample,theNetherlands-in2040.Inbothcases,thedirectionofdecarbonizationoftheoilandgassector and the understanding of the inevitability of reducingconsumptionare obvious, inconnectionwithwhichthefollowingmeasuresaretaken:● establishing specific goals, responsibilities and promoting the development of biomethane andother types of gas fromrenewable or alternative sources inheat productionandtransport (France,Italy);● optimizationofgasinfrastructureforbothtransportandstorage(Netherlands,France);● repurposing gas infrastructure for the transportation / storage of hydrogen or carbon dioxide(Netherlands)orimplementationofresearchprojectsinthisdirection(Italy).It is expedient for Ukraine to take these approaches into account during the formationof short- andmedium-termenergypolicy. The presence of significant natural gas production, the largest inthe EU,and a wide-ranging system of transportation, storage and distribution of natural gas provides bothopportunities and creates additional obstacles on the way to decarbonization in incredibly difficultconditions.Onthe one hand, inthe perioduntil2030,Ukrainewillbeabletosatisfyasignificantpartofitsenergyneeds at the expense of domesticallyproducednatural gas. Inaddition, a resource mayappear for theexport of natural gas to the EU. On the other hand, Ukraine should work to reduce natural gasconsumption, includinginfavorofgasandothertypesofenergyfromrenewableoralternativesources.Thus, policies and measures for the development of the internal market should not only apply toelectricity,butalsotogasinparticular.Thesepoliciesandmeasuresshouldgenerallyensure:● accessofgasconsumerstoreliableandaffordableenergy;● reductionofconsumptionofalltypesofenergy,includinggas;● increasingtheshareofgasfromrenewableoralternativeenergysourcesinthetotalvolumeofgasconsumption;● increasingcompetitionintherespectivemarketsandobtainingthebenefitsofliberalizedmarketsforconsumers;● creatingthenecessaryconditionsandprovidingthecorrectincentivesandsignalstothesubjectsofthenaturalgasmarkettoprepareforworkintheconditionsofadecarbonizedeconomy.

Ensuringadequacy(sufficiency)ofthepowersystem
The ESUpredicts that the growth in electricity demand will be covered primarilybycarbon-neutralsources (RESandnuclear generation). Since WPPandSPPare non-guaranteedcapacity, itsbalancinginthesystemwillbecarriedoutthrough:
● flexiblecapacitiesofHPPsandHSPs;
● balancing and reserve capacities – thermal power plants on combined fuel (natural gas and/orbiomethane)and,inthefuture,othertechnologieswithsimilartechnicalparameters;
● increasing ESS capacities, including long-term(seasonal) storage batteries using the Power-to-Xtechnology(hydrogen,ammonia,etc.).
AccordingtoESU, the total available capacityof power plants inthe UESofUkrainemayincreaseto62.9GWby2032(NPP- 17.4GW, CHP- 2.5GW,WPP-10.1GW,SPP-12.6GW,HPP–4.9GW,HSP–4.1GW, TPP–1.1GW,bioTES–0.3GW,semi-peakandpeakgeneration–9.4GW,ESS–0.5GW). Inparticular, it is predictedthat the share of nuclear generationwill remainatthelevelofabout56%inthe overall electricityproductionmixintheUESofUkrainein2050.Thecoal-firedgenerationwill be replacedbycombined-fuel CHPandTPPplants(naturalgas/biomethane)orothertechnologieswithsimilarcharacteristics.
Increasingtheflexibilityofthesystem
The UES of Ukraine does not have sufficient flexibility and will need its gradual increase toensureproper integrationof power plants withnon-guaranteedgenerationbasedonRES(solarandwind)intothesystemintheperiodupto2030andbeyond.
Accordingtothe conclusions of the 2023Generationcapacityadequacyassessmentreport,theUESofUkraine does not meet adequacy requirements, and for the further increase of power plants withnon-guaranteedgenerationbasedonRES,theproblemsofensuringoperationalsecuritywillintensify.
The commissioning of highlyflexible capacities withthe possibilityof quickramp-up(full activationfroma shutdownstate andreachingnominalpowercapacityin10-15minutes)andfast-actingreservesbasedonelectricitystorage facilities (ESS) will provide anopportunitytoprovidetheUESofUkrainewiththenecessaryregulatoryreservestomeetadequacyrequirementsinthefuture.

3.POLICIESANDMEASURES3.1.Dimensiondecarbonisation3.1.1.GHGemissionsandremovalsi. Policies and measures to achieve the economy-wide target covering all key emitting sectors andsectors for the enhancement of removals, withanoutlooktothelong-termvisionandgoaltobecomealowemission economy and achieving a balance betweenemissions andremovals inaccordance withtheParisAgreementCross-sectoralpoliciesandmeasuresPM_D_WEM_01EnvironmentaltaxleviedoncarbondioxideemissionsObjective:Stimulatingthereductionofcarbondioxideemissions(inmillionstonsofCO2),taxrevenuegenerationforthestatebudget(millionsofUAH).Legalbasis:TaxCodeofUkraine,BudgetCodeofUkraineTimeframe:since2010
Responsiblebodies/organizations:MinistryofEnvironment,MinistryofFinance,StateTaxService,SAEE
Description: Environmental taxleviedoncarbondioxideemissionsinUkrainewasintroducedin2010with the approval of the newTaxCode of Ukraine. The taxis leviedonemissions of carbondioxideintothe atmosphere bystationarysourcesofpollution.EntitiesthatemitCO2intheamountofnomorethan 500tons per year are exemptedfromthe CO2tax. Incase of exceedingthis amount, the entitiesare obliged to register as taxpayers in the tax (reporting) period, prepare and submit tax reports,calculate and pay tax for the tax (reporting) period. For entities whose annual emissions exceed500tons, the taxbase is reducedbythe amountofsuchemissionsintheamountof500tonsperyearbasedontheresultsofthetax(reporting)year.
At first, the tax rate was only 0.2 hryvnias per 1 ton of emissions andwas graduallyincreaseduntil2018. In2019, the taxrate was increasedmore than24times –fromUAH0.41/t toUAH10/t,andin2022 – another 3 times. As of 2024, the tax rate is UAH30/t. It is expected that the tax rate willcontinuetoincrease.
Withthe increase inthe taxrate, taxrevenues tothe state budget graduallyincreasedaswell.Thus,in2021, the tax brought 1.2 billion UAHto the state budget
170 
. Although the taxrate was increased3times from2022, taxrevenues increasedbyonly25%toUAH1.5billion,whichisduetoasignificantdeclineinindustrialproductionduetothefull-scaleinvasionoftheRussianFederationintoUkraine.

3.4.3.Marketintegrationi.Policiesandmeasuresrelatedtotheelementssetoutinpoint2.4.3ElectricitymarketIn 2019, Ukraine carried out a radical reformof the wholesale andretail electricitymarkets, movingfrom the "single buyer" to the EU competitive market model by introducing the appropriateinstitutional environment and structural organization of the market, providedfor bythe provisions ofthe Third EUEnergy Package. Further transformationof the electricitymarket takes place withintheframework of the Fourth EU Energy Package (Clean Energy Package). In terms of reforming anddevelopingtheelectricitymarket,Ukraineimplementsthefollowingbasicpoliciesandmeasures:● Deepening the integration with the markets of the EUandENTSO-Ecountries byincreasingthecapacityof interconnectors andintroducingEuropeanrulesforitsallocationatjointauctionsusingthe all-Europeantrade platformJoint AllocationOffice (JAO). Itisalsoplannedtocouplethespotmarkets of Ukraine and the EUcountries as soonas possible, inparticular the day-aheadmarketandtheintradaymarket(marketcoupling).● Ensuringtheproperfunctioningofthecompetitiveelectricitymarketbydeepeningitsliberalizationincombinationwithtemporaryregulatoryinterventionmeasures aimedatstabilizingthemarketatthe stage of insufficient maturity of the competitive environment andlimitedintegrationwiththemarkets of the EUandENTSO-Ecountries. At the same time,gradualharmonizationwiththeEUmarkets of spheres, methods,scopeandotherparametersofregulationisenvisaged,inparticularintermsoftheapplicationofpricecapsonthespot(DAM,IDM)andbalancingelectricitymarkets.● Development ofelectricityexchangetradingwiththeintroductionofstandardizedtradingproducts,implementation of market-based pricing in all market segments, in particular, application ofreal-timeprices,gradualeliminationofcross-subsidization.● Stimulating regulation (tariff setting) for electric network operators in order to ensure economicconditions for the modernizationanddevelopment of networkinfrastructure,introductionofsmartgrids.● Increasingthe stabilityandflexibilityof the energysystemthroughthedevelopmentofdistributedgeneration, the introduction of flexible generating capacities, energy storage facilities anddemand-side management. SECTIONB.ANALYTICALBASIS4.CURRENTSITUATIONANDPROJECTIONSWITHEXISTINGPOLICIESANDMEASURES4.1. Projected evolution of main exogenous factors influencing energy systemandGHGemissiondevelopmentsThe Russian Federation's full-scale invasion of Ukraine caused significant damage to the country'seconomy, leadingtopopulationmigration, the destructionof industrial infrastructure, a correspondingdrop in business activity, and obviously causedhighuncertaintyabout the pathof post-war recovery.The current state of the economy remains largely unknown, as most statistics are unavailable. Ingeneral, energy demand is determined by macroeconomic factors such as gross domestic product(GDP),industryoutputorvalueadded,population,andothers.Meanwhile, due to the lack of current information and the high level of uncertainty, the prospectivedynamics of the energy demand factors discussed belowcannot always be properly estimated usingtraditional approaches, but must mainly rely on assumptions and indirect information from opensources.i.Macroeconomicforecasts(GDPandpopulationgrowth)Since 2014, Ukraine's economyhas beenoperatingundertheconditionsofahybridwaroftheRussianFederation against Ukraine. But the unprovoked full-scale invasion of the Russian Federation intoUkraine, whichbeganin2022, became anewtestofthestrengthandstabilityofUkrainiansocietyandeconomy. In addition to the death and destruction Ukraine is experiencing, the economy has had toadjustto:● large-scalepopulationmigrationandadecreaseinpurchasingpower;● significantnarrowingoflogisticsroutes,narrowingoftheeconomicactivityofenterprises,includingexport-oriented;● significantshortageofelectricityincertainperiodsandblackoutschedulesintroducedinOctober2022-early2023,duringthespringof2024;● anincreaseindefensespending,whichledtoanexpansionofthestatebudgetdeficittoUAH914.9billionin2022;● sufferedhugelossesasaresultofRussianaggression,estimatedattrillionsofhryvnias.However, the successes of the defense forces of Ukraine,thecoordinatedworkoftheGovernmentandbusiness, the indomitable spirit of the population, the speedof restorationof destroyedanddamagedobjects of critical infrastructure, as well as systematic financial support frominternational partnersmadeitpossibletomaintaineconomicstability.Asaresult:● the drop in GDP turned out tobe significantlyless thanexpectedandamountedto29.1%(at thebeginning of the full-scale invasion of the Russian Federation into Ukraine, estimates variedbetween40-50%);● the increase in consumer prices also turned out to be less than expected at the beginningof thefull-scale invasionof the RussianFederationintoUkraine andrelativelycomparabletothechangeinpricesinanumberofEuropeancountries,andamountedto26.6%(annualized);● business quickly adapted to the difficult conditions and returned to work after the suspensioninFebruary-March2022ofalmost86.1%ofenterprises.So, despite all the difficulties and challenges, the economy in the conditions of military operationsmanagedtomaintainrelative macroeconomic andprice stability, toovercome thelarge-scalestoppageof productionandthe consequences of the outflowof labor resources causedbythemovementtosafeplaces.The macroeconomic forecast of NECP is based on the Forecast of the economic and socialdevelopment of Ukraine for 2024-2026 and the assumptions of the macroeconomic scenarios of the

ii.SectoralchangesexpectedtoimpacttheenergysystemandGHGemissionsThe reconstruction of destroyed infrastructure facilities (transport, energy), housing and socialinfrastructure, as well as the development of the defense-industrial complex (ODC) will become themain security priorities of Ukraine in the mediumterm. Accordingly, investments will be directedtoboth construction and equipment (military-industrial complex, energy projects, etc.), which willstimulate the development of construction, the productionof domestic machine-buildingproducts, aswellasthepurchaseofimportsforinvestmentpurposes.Onthe demandside, the driver of growthwill be investmentdemandasaresultoftheimplementationof production and infrastructure development projects and the gradual reconstruction of the affectedareas. Although this component will continue to take a leading positionamongother components ofdemand in terms of growth rates, these rates will not be sufficient to restore most of the damagedproductionfacilitiesandinfrastructureandmodernizeproductioninthecomingyears.Regarding the dynamics of the main components of GDPfromthe supplyside inthe short term, thefollowingisforecast:● The positive dynamics of the service sector will continue, whichis sensitive tothe activityof thepopulationand, givenits mobilityandthe significant level of ITuse, ismoreautonomous,aswellas quite agile and flexible to the needs of consumers, which opens up not only domestic salesmarkets. Its further development will be aimedat expandingthe arsenal of services providedwiththe helpofdigitalplatforms(includingtoEUmarkets)thankstotheimprovementofexistingortheimplementation of the latest marketing development strategies, the search for opportunities todiversifythemarketoffer,andthecreationofnewvirtualproductsandservices.● At the same time, the recoveryof industrial productionwill take place. Inthe near future, thekeytask will remain the development of effective means, methods and technologies in the field ofsecurity and defense planning to meet the priority needs of the Ukrainian army, which willstimulate the further development of mechanical engineering. The extractive industry will alsorecover relatively quickly and stably, taking into account the achievement in the perspective ofmaximum production autonomy in order to create a solid foundation for recovery during thepost-war period, whichwill make it possible tograduallymake upforthereducedpotentialoveralongperiodofdecline.

● There will be an active recovery of enterprises of the food and chemical industry, textileproduction, since their activities arerelatedtothesatisfactionofprimaryneedsandtheyaremostlyrepresentatives of small and medium-sized enterprises, which are more mobile and have wideropportunities to maneuver with logistics and sales of their products. It will be most difficult forlarge industrial enterprises, in particular metallurgical enterprises, some of which have beendestroyed. It is not so easy for such enterprises to reconfigure logistics, move their productionfacilities, andtheir restorationor the creationof completelynewmodernproductionfacilities willrequirealongerperiod.● The development of the domestic agro-industrial complexinthe forecast periodwill take placeinthe context of ensuringfoodsecurityandkeepingthe countryintheworldagriculturalrankingsasaleadingexporterofagriculturalproducts.● The needfor rapidrestorationof infrastructure (roads, bridges,communications),industrial,socialand residential facilities that have suffered significant destruction or were completely destroyedduringhostilities will require active investment inthe fieldof constructionagainstthebackgroundofmaintainingthelevelofdefensespending,whichwillcontributetoitsfurtherdevelopment.● The gradual intensificationofeconomicprocesseswillalsosupportthetransportsector,theactivityof which in most subspecies was bothstoppedduringmartial lawandsignificantlydamagedas aresult of enemyattacks. The development of the transport sector will be facilitatedbyprioritizingthe restorationoftransportinfrastructureandthedevelopmentofnewalternativetransportroutesaskey logistics channels for the supply of products to international markets. 4.4.DimensionEnergysecurityi.Currentenergymix,domesticenergyresources,importdependency,includingrelevantrisksIn recent years, the total supply of primary energy in Ukraine has been at the level of 86-93 Mtoe,which is almost a third less than in 2010. The gradual decline corresponds, on the one hand, tothedynamics of economic development/decline, andonthe other hand, toanincrease inthe efficiencyofenergyconversionandconsumption.At the same time, import indicators were quite stable. As of 2020, imports amountedto30.7Mtoe,orabout 35%of the total sources of primary energysupply. The share of ownproductioninTPESwas65%in2020,anddidnotexceed70%intheprevious5years.

4.5.DimensionInternalenergymarket4.5.1.Electricityinterconnectivityi.CurrentinterconnectionlevelandmaininterconnectorsUkraine has direct electricity connections with the ENTSO-Ecountries andMoldova. Until February24, 2022, due to the technical features of Ukraine's energy system, there were two separate tradingzones: Island of Burshtyn TPP (synchronized with ENTSO-E) and United Energy System(UES) ofUkraine (synchronized with the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus). Inorder totest thestability of the energy systeminpreparationfor integrationwiththe energysystems of the ENTSO-Ecountries, since February 24, the UES of Ukraine was disconnectedfromthe systems of the RussianFederationandtheRepublicofBelarus,andtheinternalsystems(tradezones)weresynchronized.FromMarch16, 2022, the unifiedtradezoneoftheUESofUkrainefunctionssimultaneouslywithelectricitysystemsofcontinentalEuropeENTSO-E.The taskof integratingthe UESof Ukraine intoENTSO-Ehas beencompleted, at the same time,itisnecessary to additionally implement technical measures to eliminate the insufficient damping oflow-frequency interregional power fluctuations involving the energy systems of Ukraine andMoldova.
414
414
Accordingtotheconclusionsofthereport"DynamiccalculationsforasynchronousinterconnectionofthegridsofContinentalEuropeandUkraine/Moldovausingthepresentnetwork"oftheENTSO-EConsortium

4.5.2.Energytransmissioninfrastructurei.KeycharacteristicsoftheexistingtransmissioninfrastructureforelectricityandgasElectricityinfrastructureThe UES of Ukraine is a set of power plants, electric networks, and other electric power facilitiesunitedbyacommonmodeofproduction,transmissionand

distributionof electricitywithcentralizedcontrol of this mode. The UESofUkraineisthebasisofthecountry's electricity sector, which provides centralized electricity supply to domestic consumers,interacts withthe energysystems of neighboringcountries, andensurestheexportingandimportingofelectricity. It combines generating capacities, distribution networks of the regions of Ukraine,connectedtoeachotherby220-750kVtransmissionlines(electricitytransmissionsystem).UES of Ukraine is one of the largest energy associations in Europe; it includes 6 regional powersystemsand32DSOs.Dispatching,balancemaintenanceintheUESofUkraineandtheorganizationofsynchronous operation with the energysystems of ENTSO-Emember countries are performedbythetransmissionsystemoperator(TSO)NECUkrenergo.System-forming networks with a voltage of 220-750 kVinclude trunk and cross-border lines. Theyensure the production of electricity frompowerful units of power plants and its transmission to thedistribution networks of the regions of Ukraine (electricity distribution systems), as well asinterconnections with the energy systems of neighboringcountries. Power transformationis providedusing autotransformers and transformers with a voltage of 750/500 kV, 750/330 kV, 500/220 kV,330/220kV, 400/330kV, 330/110(150) kV, 220/110(150) kV, 150/110kV.AsofJanuary1,2021,TSOhas21,861.6kmofoverheadlines(OHL)inoperationalongtheroute,and23,559.1km-alongchains.Accordingtothe TransmissionSystemDevelopment Planfor 2022-2031, as ofthebeginningof2021,there were 141substations witha voltage of 110-750kVandatransformercapacityof83,178.1MVAonthe TSObalance sheet. Substations 220kV–33units,330kV–88units,400kV–2units,500kV–3units, 750kV–9units and110kV- 6units (stationnodes of solar power plants). Suchastatesignificantlyaffectstheincreaseinlosses of electricityinthe transmissionsystemandlimits thepossibilityofpreventingtechnologicalviolations - damage toelectrical equipment or violations of its performance,whichleadstoaviolationofthenormalandreliableoperationofelectricpowerfacilitiesandUESofUkraineasawhole.

As a result of changes in climatic conditions in recent decades, a significant number of powertransmission lines built in the 1970s and 1980s are vulnerable toincreasedclimatic loads. Toa largeextent, this is evident in the autumn-winter period in the southern and northern regions of Ukraine(Southern, Dnipro and Northern energy systems). Due to increased loads and the effects of stormywind, icing,vibrationandgallopingofwires,thenumberofdamagetotheOHLelementshasincreasedsignificantly and their wear has accelerated. As a result, there was a needfor fundamental technicalre-equipment and reconstruction of OHLof the specified regions and in general, since the designoperationallife(40years)ofmostofthemhasalreadyexpired.The need for reconstruction of the 220 kVsubstation of UES of Ukraine remains urgent, since theoperational life of most of them already exceeds 50 years. The annual plans include repairs to thefoundations of metal supports, reinforcedconcrete supports, replacement oflightningprotectioncable,porcelain insulation and other works aimed at ensuringthe reliabilityof the OHL. At the same time,due tothe acceleratedwear andtear oftheOHLandtheimpactofincreasedloads,theseworksrequireevermoreannualmaterialandlaborresources.The analysis of financing and implementation of capital repair, technical re-equipment andreconstruction of OHL shows that the amount of restoration does not reduce the existing disparitybetween wear and tear and restoration and does not fix the issue of considerable wear and tear ofnetworks.

Onthe one hand,Ukraine was able to prove a high level of sustainability and resilience of the energy systemby theoperation for three weeks in an isolated mode and joining ENTSO-E, and in June - by startingcommercialelectricityexportstotheEU.On the other hand, massive missile and drone attacks on energy infrastructure caused significantdestructionanddamage togenerationfacilities andelectrical networks. Since March2024, Russiahasresumedlarge-scalecombinedattacksontheenergyinfrastructureof the UESof Ukraine, focusingthemprimarilyonflexible generation-TPPsandHPPs.AnumberoflargeCHPsofregionalimportancewerealsodestroyed.Due tothe large-scale migrationof the populationabroadandthereductionofproductionandbusinessactivity, the demand for electricityinthe power systemdecreasedbyapproximately30-35%. defines two categories of transport: freight andpassenger. Projections of development withexistingpolicies andmeasuresatleastuntil2040(includingfortheyear2030)ElectricitymarketAmong the key factors that will determine the situation on the electricitymarket of Ukraine andthepotential offoreigntradeafterthecancellationorterminationofmartiallaw,itisworthhighlightingthefollowing:1. the extent of damage and destruction of generation facilities and electrical networks, whichwilldetermine the volume, composition, flexibilityofelectricitysupply,aswellasthelevelofpricesinthedomesticmarket;2. dynamics of recoveryof economic activityandsocio-demographicdynamicsinthecountry,whichwill determine the volume andcompositionof demandfor electricity, as well as the consumptionprofile(loadcurve);3. pricecapregulationandothertypesofregulationinwholesalemarketsegments;4. the policy of bringing electricity prices for households to a market-based level along with thegradualminimizationofPSOandincreasingthesupplyofelectricityinthecompetitivemarket;5. deepening integration with the markets of EU countries (increasing cross-border capacity andintegration), in particular, by combining day-ahead and intraday markets (market coupling) withEasternEuropeancountries(Poland,Romania,Slovakia,HungaryandMoldova).


Takingintoaccount the factors of significant inflation, we canexpectagradualincreaseinthelevelofmarginal prices (price caps)ofelectricityinthewholesalemarketsegments(DAM,IDMandbalancingmarket). The revisionof price caps maycause acorrespondingincreaseinwholesaleelectricityprices,includingintheBCMsegment,whichyetfocusesonDAMreferencepricequotes.Prices for households remainedatthecurrentleveluntiltheendofthe2023/2024heatingseason.Theirupward revision during the martial lawin Ukraine is possible - providedthere is a slight multi-stageincrease over time (at leastfor2-3years).TheCabinetofMinistersofUkrainewilladopttheRoadmapfor the gradual liberalization of the gas and electricity markets with the steps to be taken and thecorresponding terms to be implemented after the end of martial law. The roadmap will be basedontechnicalanalysistounderstandthefinancialstateofthesector.As part of the deepening of the European integration of markets, Market Operator joined theCommittee of European Market Operators (NEMO Committee) in the status of an observer of theoperation of the EU spot electricity market - SDAC(single day-ahead coupling) and SIDC(SingleIntradayCoupling). The status of the observer allowstostartthetechnicalpreparationforthecouplingofthespotmarketsofUkraineandEuropeancountries.
465
The planned interconnectors’ development of UESof Ukraine withthe ENTSO-EenergysystemandUkraine's full participationinthe coupledspot markets of EasternEuropeancountries will expandtheopportunities for the development of cross-border electricity trade, which will be limited by theavailable capacity of interconnectors. As a result, a gradual convergence of prices on the wholesaleelectricity market of Ukraine and the markets of Eastern European countries is expected. Thedirections, time periods and volume of cross-border trade will be determined depending marketconditions on the coupledelectricitymarkets. Inaddition, the possibilityof exportingelectricityfromUkrainetotheEUcountrieswillbeinfluencedbythefactorofapplicationoravoidanceoftheCBAM.NaturalgasmarketExistingpolicies andmeasures generallydonot allowachievingall the goals definedforthe"Internalenergymarket-gas"dimension.First, the presence of restrictions onthe export of bothnatural gas andbiomethanesignificantlylimitsdomestic productionanddistorts prices onthe domestic market. Inthecontextofbiomethane,thisbanreduces the pressure on the sector to overcome other problems faced by biomethane producers (forexample, problems with access to networks): in the case of the opening of exports, these problemswouldbecomemoreurgentandtheirresolutionwouldbeaccelerated.Secondly, the presence of price restrictions (under PSOregulations) for a large number of consumersalso does not encourage an increase in production, including due to the development of newtechnologies and the search for synergies. In addition, such restrictions - against the background ofreducedconsumptiondue tomilitaryactions - leadtothe weakeningof competitiondue toadecreasein the volume of imports and importers who usually compete with sellers of gas from their ownproduction.Thirdly, without the introduction of additional measures, the working conditions inthe domestic gasmarket are difficultandonerousfornewplayers.Thisconcernstheuncertaintyregardingthefateoftheproperty and assets of the GDS, the insufficient level of their unbundlingfromthe interests of supplyandproduction, as well as the lackof guarantees ofadequatefinancing,whichhasasignificantimpactontheoperationoftheretailmarket.Dependentonthisarealsotheproblemsofbalancingrulesandthelack of a comprehensive system of commercial gas accounting (on the background of insufficientequipment of consumers with meteringdevices), which, under existingpolicies andmeasures, donotallowsupplierstoindependently

iv.Descriptionofenergysubsidies,includingforfossilfuels
In Ukraine, there are several types of direct and indirect subsidies onstate-regulatedenergymarkets(gas, electricity, district heating). The system of energy subsidies in Ukraine is primarily aimed atprotecting vulnerable households that can be characterized as energy poor. However, the biggestbeneficiaries of this systemare wealthycitizens. This is a result of the fact that the systemof energysubsidiesinthementionedmarketsconsistsofseverallevels:1. Differenttariffsforhouseholdsandlegalentities.Inthegas,districtheatingandelectricitymarkets,there are preferentialprices/tariffsforhouseholds(domesticconsumers)andmarketpricesforlegalentities.Separatepreferentialprices/tariffsalsoexistforreligiousorganizations;2. Targeted Subsidies for Vulnerable Consumers allow financial assistance to be provided tohouseholds whose utility costs exceed a percentage of their monthly income set by theGovernment.Typical mechanisms that allow setting prices/tariffs for domestic consumers (households) at a levellowerthaneconomicallyreasonableareasfollows:● Cross-subsidization at the expense of the income of electricity producers, determined by theCabinet of Ministers ofUkrainewithintheframeworkofthemechanismofimposingspecialdutieson individual market participants to ensure public interest (PSO) - for example, inthe electricitymarket;● Reimbursement through co-financing of state-owned companies involved in PSOfromthe statebudget(forexample,onthegasmarket);● Supportforheatproducersfromlocalbudgets.TerminologicalremarksIt is worthnotingthat there are several interpretations of subsidies inthe legal frameworkofUkraine,inparticular, a number of different terms are usedinrelationtobudgetpolicyandstatesupport.Thesetermscanbecomparedtocomponentsofthebroaderdefinitionsusedbyinternationalorganizations.Adirect and rather narrowdefinitionof subsidies is giveninthe Instructiononthe applicationof theeconomic classification of budget expenditures
483 
, approved by order of the Ministry of FinanceNo.333of March12,2012.Accordingtotheinstruction,subsidiesaredefinedas"allgratuitouscurrentpayments to enterprises that do not provide for compensation in the form of specially stipulatedpayments or goods and services in exchange for payments made, as well as expenses related tocompensationforlossesofstate
483

enterprises". The budget legislation of Ukraine contains the concepts of subventions, subsidies andothertransfers,whichcanbeconsideredsubsidiesaccordingtointernationaldefinitions.The Lawof Ukraine "OnState AidtoBusinessEntities"
484
definesthatstateaidissupportinanyformto economic entities at the expense of state or local resources, which distorts or threatens to distorteconomic competition, creating advantages for production certain types of goods or the conduct ofcertaintypes of economic activity. Thislawalsodefinesthatstateaidconsistsinthetransferofstateorlocal resources to individual economic entities, as well as in the loss of revenues of the relevantbudgets. The forms of state aid include, in particular: the provision of subsidies and grants, theprovisionof subsidies, the provisionof taxbenefits, the postponement or deferment ofthepaymentoftaxes,feesorothermandatorypayments.Also, since May16, 2008, Ukraine isamemberoftheWorldTradeOrganization(WTO),thereforethedefinition "subsidy" given in the Agreement on Subsidies and Compensatory Measures (SCCAgreement)

5.2. Macroeconomic and, to the extent feasible, the health, environmental, employment andeducation,skills and social impacts, including just transition aspects (in terms of costs and benefits as well ascost-effectiveness) of the plannedpolicies andmeasures describedinsection3atleastuntilthelastyearof the period covered by the plan, including comparison to projections with existing policies andmeasuresAt this stage, the assessment of the impact of the implementationof the scenarios withexistingpoliciesandmeasures (WEM) andplannedpolicies andmeasures (WAM) onmacroeconomic indicators was notcarried out. However, an analogy can be drawn with the study of the macroeconomic impact of theimplementation of the scenarios of the updated Nationally Determined Contribution of Ukraine to theParis Agreement, which was carried out within the framework of the EBRDproject "Support to theGovernment of Ukraine for the Update of the NDC"
501 
and is described in detail in the IEPModelingReport of the National Academyof Sciences of the RussianAcademyof Sciences
502
. Accordingtothisstudy, among the policy implementation options analyzed, the path of intensive investments in energyefficiency technologies is the most attractive bothfromthe point of viewof macroeconomics andfromsectoral perspectives. Inthe case of implementationof suchanoption, there aresignificantbenefitsbothfor the economy and for the surrounding natural environment. With higher levels of investment andimprovements inenergyefficiencyandrelativelylowpricesforGHGemissionreductionsby2035-2040,GDPwill growat a faster rate. At the same time, after 2035, due toa higher levelofambitiontoreduceGHGemissions anda correspondingincrease inthecarbonprice,additionalGDPgrowthrateswillslow.Household incomes will be similar. The populationwill face a higher level of carbonprices, whichwillaffect their purchasing power. At the same time, evenduringthe periodof 2040-2050, whenthe carbonprice will exceed the level of 100 USD/ton of CO2-eq., the population will still see anincrease inthelevel of real incomes compared to the baseline scenario. Improvements inenergyefficiencyplaya keyrole in making this happen, with significant reductions in the cost of production and correspondinglylowerpricesforend-usersinhouseholds.Also, with the implementationof ambitious energyandclimate scenarios, significant transformations inthe structure of productioncanbe observed, whichleads tosignificant reductionsinGHGemissionsandthe energy intensity of GDP. This is particularly the case in scenarios withhighcarbonprices, suchascoke and coal production/mining, which could fall by more than 75%in 2050. Other energy-intensivesectors such as metallurgical production, petrochemicals, utilities and metal processing can alsosignificantly reduce their production. At the same time, there is a reorientation towards sectors thatgenerate investments and relevant services. The latter include increasedproductioninthe programmingand research sector. The construction sector is increasing production as a keysupplier of the means ofproductionof goods. The increase intheproductionoffoodproductsandtheagriculturalsectorismostlycausedbytheincreaseintheexportofthesegoods.Figure 5.25illustrates reductions inpollutant emissions under the WEMandWAMscenarios.Duetotheimplementationof the NERPandthe decommissioningofcoal-firedpowerunitsofthermalpowerplantsandthermal power plants, emissions of pollutants fromlarge combustionplants disappear, whichcannotfail to have a positive effect on the state of the natural environment and the health of the population,reducing the risks of diseases of the respiratory and circulatory system, reducing vulnerability torespiratoryviralinfections.

The decisive factor that will contribute tothe implementationofreformsandenergy-efficientmeasuresbythepopulationistheintroductionofmarketpricesforenergy.Currently, electricitytariffs for the populationare set administratively, prices for natural gasandthermalenergyare alsoregulatedandfixednot higherthanthecorrespondinglevelsonFebruary24,2022duringthe periodof martial lawinUkraine andsixmonths after its cancellation.However,theGovernmenthaslimited opportunities to liberalize prices in view of the drop in incomes of the population due to thefull-scale invasionoftheRussianFederationinUkraine:accordingtotheresultsof2022,realwageshavedecreased by 11.4%. At the same time, there are still risks of damage or destruction of buildingsthroughout the territory of Ukraine, which also contributes to the postponement of the demandfor theimplementationofenergy-efficientmeasuresforthepost-warperiod.Lackof qualifiedpersonnel.Theneedforreconstructionbasedonthe"BuildBackBetter"principle,theimplementationof energyefficiencyimprovement policies (localenergyplans,implementationofenergymanagement systems), the development of new production chains in the climate innovation andrenewable energysectors increase the demandforqualifiedpersonnel.Atthesametime,themobilizationtothe ArmedForcesofUkraine,aswellasthedepartureofasignificantnumberofthepopulationoutsideof Ukraine as a result of the full-scale invasion of the Russian Federation into Ukraine, are alreadycreatingashortageofworkerswhocouldimprovetheirqualificationsoracquireanewspecialty.iii. analysis of additional public finance support or resources tofillidentifiedgapsidentifiedunderpointiiPossibilities of additional support fromthe State Budget of Ukraine are extremely limited. During theperiod of martial law, the directions of the state budget policyare focusedonthe redistributionof statebudget funds in order to support the key needs of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, ensure the country'sdefensecapability,andimplementmeasurestoensurenationalsecurity.Thus,thereisalackoffundseventofinanceexistingeconomicprograms.Clause12oftheMeasuresregardingtheeffectiveandrationaluseof state funds, provided for the maintenance of state authorities andother state institutions, enterprises,institutions andorganizations establishedbystate authorities, whichuse state budget funds,approvedbythe Resolutionof the Cabinet ofMinistersofUkraineofOctober11,2016No.710"OntheEffectiveUseof State Funds" (Official Gazette ofUkraine,2016,No.83,Article2739;2019,No.47,Article1608,No.94, Article 3098; 2022, No. 10, Article 531; 2024, Article 2687) provides for the suspension of thepreparation of new state programs or the introduction of changes to the approved state budget. Thecondition for the inclusionof exceptions tothe Measures is the provisioninnewprograms of financingfromthestatebudgetstartingfromthesecondbudgetperiodaftertheabolitionofmartiallawinUkraine.Budgetaryfinancingof state targetedeconomic programs canbe consideredat the expense of grants forbudget support from foreign countries, foreign financial institutions and international financialorganizations (including grants for achievingperformance indicators), income fromassistance programsand grants of the European Union, governments of foreigncountries, international organizations, donorinstitutions, as well as credits (loans) received by the state from foreign countries, foreign financialinstitutions andinternational financialorganizationsfortheimplementationofinvestmentprojects.Atthesame time, inaccordance withthe requirements of the legislation, theimplementationofstateborrowingand management of the state debt, the provision of state guarantees is carried out under a number of

conditions and is limited - especially in circumstances when Ukraine does not have full access to theinternationalborrowingmarketandhasalimitedresourceofthedomesticmarket.Similarly, the resources of localbudgetsarealsoquitelimited,andtheiravailabilitydependsonanumberof factors - economic activityinthe territoryof the relevant territorial community, financial capacityofthe local government, etc. Local borrowingandlocaldebtmanagement,provisionoflocalguaranteesarealsosubjecttoanumberofconditionsandlimitations.Thus, support must come fromother sources not prohibited by law. These are, in particular, investors'funds (due to the introduction of market mechanisms to stimulate them, simplification of permittingprocedures, other non-fiscalformsofsupport),grantprograms,otheravailablefinancialinstruments(e.g.,syndicated loans guaranteed by foreign states, foreign financial institutions, and international financialorganizations , bonds issued by them, other forms of mixed financing), especially of a targetednature(e.g., climate financing). GasmarketPlanned policies and measures will ensure conditions for cross-border movement of gas (natural gas,biomethane) across Ukraine's border with EU and Energy Community Contracting Parties. Accordingly, comfortable conditions shouldbe createdonthe domestic market for thesaleofdomesticallyproducedgas.Tothisend,theplannedmeasuresinclude,ontheonehand,theliberalizationofgasprices(simultaneouslywiththerenewalofthesystemofhousingsubsidies, the creation of a systemfor the protection of vulnerable consumers and the monitoring andreduction of energy poverty), and on the other hand, the improvement of the conditions of access ofsellers tothe functioningwholesale market andtoretail market(improvementoftherulesofcommercialaccounting,balancing,reformsofGDS).In addition, the planned policies and measures will enable the existingenergyinfrastructure toadapt tonew conditions, with an emphasis on deeper integration into political, research, design and businessprocesses inthe EU. This, inturn, will make itpossibletoreducetheburdenofcostsforthecreationandtransformationof infrastructure onUkrainianconsumers, as well asincreaseincomefromforeignbuyersofservicesofenergyinfrastructurefacilities.According to the results of modeling using the TIMES-Ukraine model, natural gas production fordomestic consumption may be sufficient at the level of 19-20 bcm, after which, with more intensiveimplementationof decarbonizationmeasures, inparticular a significant increase inthe price of CO2andexpansion of the productionof renewable gases (primarilybiomethane), gas productionwill decrease to11.4bcmin2050(Fig. 5.31). The marginal price fornaturalgasundertheWAMscenariosmaybelowerthanthe correspondingprice inthe WEMscenariosince the demandfor natural gas will be lowerintheWAMscenario(Fig.5.32).At the same time, biomethane productionwill increase from0.9bcmin2030toalmost 10bcmin2050and will mainly be consumed in the domestic market, reaching exports of 1.9 bcmin 2050. Insteadhydrogenproductionmayreach1.0bcmin2035andgrowto5.0bcm,butunlikebiomethane,almostallofitwillbeexportedtoEUcountries.

Norms ofdirect application are norms that can be the legal basis for the claims of individuals and legal entitiesregardingthe recognitionof their rights bothtothe state (verticaldirectapplication)andtootherpersons(horizontal direct application). The normofdirectapplicationcanbecontainedinalaw,aby-law,aswellas (in some cases) an international treaty. However, not every normof the law, by-lawor internationaltreaty is a norm of direct application. The norm has direct application if it is specific, clear andunconditional, as well as if it does not require additional implementation measures fromthe state. Thestatus of a norm of direct application is determined by analyzing a specific normon the basis of thespecified criteria. In the context of Ukraine, an example of a norm of direct application can be theprovision of the lawonthe effect of the principle of non-discriminationinrelations betweensubjects ofenergymarkets. Norms of directapplicationarenotnormsthatdeterminethegoalsorgeneraltasksofthestate, its bodies or other persons, define a wide range of discretion in their application or requireadditionalimplementationactions.Thirdly, given the relatively small number of norms of direct application in the energy legislation ofUkraine, as well as the legal uncertainty regarding the direct application of norms fromthe acts of theEnergyCommunity, the implementedpolicies andmeasures willprimarilyincludepoliciesandmeasuresregardingwhich:a) "one or more voluntary agreements have been concluded" (that is, the policy or measure isimplementednot inpursuance of a legal norm, but ofaconcludedagreementthatmustbeimplemented),orb) "allocated financial resources" (i.e., relevant costs included in the tariff of regulatedmarket entities,allocatedfromthestatebudgetorfromfundsofinternationalfinancialassistance,etc.),orc)mobilizedhumanresources.With regard to concluded agreements, the agreements themselves are taken into account, and notmemorandaofunderstandingorlettersofintent.

ContinuationofAppendix1tothePlanWith regard to the allocation of financial resources, the presence of an approved, sufficiently clearfinancing mechanismfor relevant policies or measures is takenintoaccount, whichcanbe the basis forthe formation of legal requirements of the parties (for example, the funds are includedinthe tariff, theright to conclude a purchase and sale agreement at the green tariff / tax discount / a reduced tax ratedeterminedbylegislation, andthere are noregulatoryrestrictions for its implementation,etc.).Problemswith the application of such mechanisms (for example, non-payment byparties, accumulationof debts,etc.) can be taken into account for the recognition of the status of policies and measures only inexceptionalcases.The implementedpolicies andmeasures are closelyrelatedtothe adoptedpolicies andmeasures astheyare combinedwithina single set of existingpolicies andmeasures. The criteria for adoptedpolicies andmeasures are: a) "anofficial government decisionhas beenadopted"andb)"thereisaclearcommitmenttofurtherimplementation."Given that the executive branch of government usually adopts specific policies and measures, and theGovernment is its representative, the referencetotheexistenceofagovernmentdecisiondoesnotmeanarestriction on the decision-making body (ie, not only the Government can make such a decision), butrather indicates tothe specificityandrealismof policies andmeasuresbelongingtothegroupofadoptedand, accordingly, existing policies and measures. At the same time, the adoption of a norm by theparliament onits owninitiative(intheabsenceoftheGovernment'sinitiative)canbeanindicatorthatthepolicy or measure cannot be related to the adopted and existing ones, in particular, in the case ofnon-fulfillmentofthesecondcriterion.The criterionof havinga "clear commitment tofurtherimplementation"isinterpretedasfollows:ifthereisalegalbasisfortherelevantpolicyandmeasure,thenecessaryactionsandresourcesareclearlydefinedfor its implementation, andthere is anunderstandingthat these resources shouldbe allocated. The closeconnection with implemented policies and measures indicates that in the case of adopted policies andmeasures, it is preciselya clearcommitmenttoallocatefinancialresources,mobilizehumanresources,orbereadytoenterintovoluntaryagreements.Fourth, itshouldbenotedthatplannedpoliciesandmeasuresreferto'options' (not'policiesandmeasures'asinthepreviousdefinitions).Two criteria are put forwardfor these options: a) beingat the discussionstage; andb) "a real chance ofbeingadoptedandimplementedafterthedateofsubmission."ConsideringtheterminologyoftheEnglishversion, discussions donotmeanformalpublicdiscussions,butmostlythepresenceofadiscussionoftherelevant option in public circles. The existence of a discussion is presumed if it is about policies andmeasuresthatareplannedinresponsetoanalreadyadoptedactofhigherlegalforce(law).The second criterion is restrictive in terms of the range of all possible options under discussion. Inthiscase,severalcasesareaccepted,whichindicatetherealism(“realchance”)oftheoptions.Thefirstcaseisthe option announcement level: it is taken into account that policies and measures can be consideredrealistic under the condition of official announcement by such state officials as the President, PrimeMinister, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister, Head or Deputy Heads of the Office President, under theconditions of their sufficient detail and objective realism. The second case is the presence of specificexternal factors that clearly encourage the implementation of policies and measures. These externalfactors can be both part of Ukraine's international obligations and contained in the legislationof othercountries. To identify such external factors, it is not enoughthat theyare part of Ukraine's internationalobligations. In addition to formal obligation, the factor of high risk of sanctions or other negativeconsequences from non-fulfillment of obligations or other third-party conditions (for example,non-provisionof funds, refusal topurchase products, etc.) shouldbeadded.ExamplesofthesecondcasecanbeCBAM,EUrequirementsforgreenhydrogen,sustainabilityofbiofuels,etc.

Appendix2tothePlanGHGemissionsinagricultureandassumptionsaboutthemainparametersofagriculturaldevelopmentInagriculture, the emissions ofthreegreenhousegasses(methane(CH4),nitrogen(I)oxide(N2O)andcarbon(IV) oxide (СО2))areconsidered,theemissionsofwhicharearesultofaneconomicactivityintwosectors-livestockandcropproduction.Animal husbandry is characterized by two processes, which are accompanied by the emission ofmainlymethaneand,inarelativelysmallamount,nitrogen(I)oxide:intestinal(orenteral)fermentationofagriculturalanimals(mainlycattle);handlingofdroppingsandmanureoffarmanimals.Crop production has a much more complex organization and is characterized by the emissionof allthreegreenhousegassesinthefollowingprocesses:● N2O: applicationof nitrogen(mineral) fertilizers; applicationof organic fertilizers; applicationoforganic fertilizers from livestock grazing; introduction of nitrogen (N) with crops residues;mineralizationor immobilizationof nitrogen(N) associatedwiththe movement of organic matterinthesoil;cultivationoforganicsoils;weatheringofnitrogen(N);leachingofnitrogen(N);● CH4:ricecultivation;● СО2:applicationofurea;limingofsoils.The keyfactors that determine the dynamics of greenhouse gas emissionsinanimalhusbandryarethenumber of farmanimals andthe manure management system, whichis usedtocollect,transport,storeand use manure. The manure management systemas a separate factor that regulates the amount ofgreenhouse gas emissions bothbytheamountofmanureenteringitandbythetypeofsysteminwhichthis manure is collected, transported, stored and used. The following types of manure managementsystems are mainly used in the livestock industry of Ukraine: solid storage system; liquid manurestorage system; storage system in open anaerobic lagoons; aerobic treatment system; composting;manure/excrementleftonpasture,paddocks,etc.The fieldof cropproductioninagriculture is multifaceted, andtherefore it is impossible tosingleoutgeneral key factors that would determine the dynamics of greenhouse gas emissions in all or mostprocesses-onlyspecialones,namely:applicationofnitrogen(mineral)fertilizers
–amountofnitrogen(mineral)fertilizersappliedtoarablesoils;applicationoforganicfertilizers –amountoforganicfertilizersappliedtoarablesoils;applicationoforganicfertilizersfromlivestockgrazing
–theamountofdroppingsleftonthegrazingfieldsofagriculturalanimals;applicationofNwiththeremainsoffieldcrops
– the amount of N in plant residues (and, accordingly, theamount of residues themselves) that remaininthe fields afterharvestingandareplowedintothesoil;cultivationoforganicsoils –theareaoforganicsoilssetasideforfieldcrops;mineralizationor immobilizationofNassociated with the movement oforganicmatterinthesoil
–the amount of Nlost as a result of soilmanagement(tillage,fertilization,plowingofplantresidues,etc.);

ContinuationofAppendix2tothePlan
weatheringN –theamountofNappliedtothesoilfromvarioussources;leachingN –theamountofNappliedtothesoilfromvarioussources;ricecultivation –theareaofagriculturalsoilsdevotedtoriceandtheamountofappliedorganicfertilizers;applicationofurea –amountofureaappliedtoarablesoils;limingofsoils -theamountofusedlimingmaterials.

Appendix3tothePlanMethodologyformodelingthedevelopmentoftheenergysystemofUkraineintheTIMES-UkrainemodelThe TIMES-Ukrainemodelisalinearoptimizationmodeloftheenergysystem(ofthe"bottom-up"type),whichdescribesindetailallenergyflowsinUkraine
514
.In the TIMES-Ukraine model, the energy systemof Ukraine is divided into seven sectors (Fig. D3.1),which includes all energy flows from the extraction of primary energy resources to their finalconsumption with intermediate stages of transformation (processing, production of secondary energyresources, etc.) , import, export andtransportation. This corresponds tothe methodological approachofthe State of the Union, which, in turn, is harmonized withthe relevant methodologies of the EuropeanCommission(Eurostat)andtheInternationalEnergyAgency(IEA).TIMES-type models contain a significant number of technologies in different sectors of the energysystem, providing information about different types of energy, technologies, etc. Currently, theTIMES-Ukraine model includes almost 2,000technologies, bothexistinginUkraine andthose thatexiston international markets andcanbe implementedinUkraine. The sources of data for cost andtechnicalcharacteristics arethematerialsoftheIEA,theDanishEnergyAgency(DEA),theNationalLaboratoryofRenewable EnergySources (NREL), specializedassociations inUkraine, scientific institutes,andenergycompanies.The TIMES-Ukraine model complies withthe methodological recommendations of theSecretariatoftheUNFrameworkConventiononClimate Change regardingthe development ofenergyandenvironmentalforecasts
515 
. A recent model is capable of achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across theeconomy,whichhasbeenhighlightedinanumberofpeer-reviewedpublications

The database of the TIMES-Ukraine model is filled with economic and energy data for 2005-2020, aswell as estimates of the correspondingdata for 2022, takingintoaccounttheirchangesinthefuture.Themainsources of the database are statistical observations oftheStateStatisticsService,theNationalBankof Ukraine, data fromUkrainianministries anddepartments, housingandcommunal enterprises, energygeneratingandenergysupplycompanies, specializedassociations, academicinstitutions,etc.Inaddition,data frominternational organizations (MEA, IAEA, OECD, IMF, WorldBank, UN, etc.) are usedinthepartofenergyandeconomicdevelopmentforecasting.Energy systemmodels, such as TIMES-Ukraine, are commonly used for long-termanalysis of energysystemdevelopment pathways aroundthe world,includingwidespreadintheEuropeanUnionatboththepan-European and national levels. By changing assumptions about useful energy demand, technology,prices or other external variables, numerous scenarios can be created and analyzed, includingdecarbonisation scenarios for the buildings sector. First, a scenario (or a set of scenarios) is developedwithout the introduction of relevant measures (Baseline, Business As Usual scenario), and in the nextstep, policy scenarios are developed (for example, policies to increase energy efficiency, developrenewable energysources(RES)orreduceGHG,decarbonization)byoverlayingadditionalrestrictionsorgoals for the energysystem(or itscomponent,suchasthebuildingsector)toassesstheimpact(effect)ofthe implementationof the policies under study. The result of the simulationis the evaluationoftheleastexpensivesolutionsfortheentireenergysystemunderthegivenconditionsandrestrictions.The TIMES-Ukraine model was used to prepare a number of strategic documents approved by theGovernment of Ukraine in2016-2021, inparticular: National EnergyEfficiencyActionPlans until2020and for 2019-2030; Ukraine's expectedNationallyDeterminedContributiontothe Paris Agreement andits updatedversion; Strategies for low-carbondevelopment of Ukraine until 2050, Strategies forthermalmodernisationofbuildingsinUkraineuntil2050,etc.In recent years, the Institute of Economics and Forecasting of the National Academy of Sciences ofUkraine has been applying and developing this model in cooperation with US national laboratories, inparticular with the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, the National Renewable Energy Laboratory(NREL), Argonne National Laboratory(Argonne National Laboratory) andLawrence BerkeleyNationalLaboratory (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory) as part of the Net Zero World initiative. Forexample, in December 2023, at COP28 in Dubai, as part of the programof the Ukrainianpavilion, theresults of modeling the post-war low-carbon development of the Ukrainian energy industry

Appendix4tothePlanMethodologyforforecastingGHGemissionsinthewastemanagementsectorThe assessment of GHGemissionsinthewastemanagementsectorwascarriedoutinaccordancewiththeprinciples and methodologies of the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National GHG Gas Inventories
523
(hereinafter referred to as the 2006 IPCCGuidelines), therefore the sources of GHGemissions do notcorrespondtothe types of economic activity, but tothe categories recommendedintheabove-mentionedmethodologies (IPCCcategories ) inthe "Waste" sector. Accordingly, emissions fromthemanagementofagricultural residues, as well as relevant GHGemissionreductionpolicies,weretakenintoaccounteitherin the LULUCF sector or in the energy sector, if such policies were accompanied by useful energyproduction. GHGemissions that are accompaniedbythe beneficial use ofenergyduringwastetreatment,such as biogas recovery at landfills, as well as energyproductionat waste incinerationplants andwasteincineration in cement production, have been taken into account in the Energy sector, but the effect ofreducingGHGemissionsasaresultofcarryingoutthecorrespondingactivitiesweretakenintoaccountinthe waste management sector. The assessment of GHGemissions inthe"Waste"sectorwascarriedoutinstrict accordance withthe methods andtakingintoaccounttheemissionfactorsusedtoreport
524
Ukraine'snational GHG emissions within the framework of obligations under the UN Convention on ClimateChangeandtheParisAgreement.Forexample,theassessmentofmethaneemissionsduetowastedisposalin landfills was carried out using the first-order decay method, as recommended in the 2006 IPCCGuidelines.General assumptions and methodological principles for determining data on activities in the"Waste" sector. The following indicators andtrends were usedduringmodelinginthe Waste sector bycategory,wheresector-specificindicatorsarehighlightedinitalics:Disposal of solid waste: population, specific volumes of solid waste generation (domestic waste) perinhabitant, waste management practices (proportion of disposal, reuse, recycling, composting,incineration), coverage of the population by the systemof centralized waste collection, construction ofnewsanitary (deepmanaged) landfills,compositionoflandfills,proportionofflaringandbiogasrecoveryatlandfills.In order to ensure the principle of transparency, the model of the mass balance of householdwaste usedduring the modeling of GHGemissions in the "Waste" sector is showninFigure A2.1, fromwhichthefollowingbasicprovisionsofmathematicalmodelingfollow:1. The total amount of generatedhouseholdwaste corresponds tothe amount of officiallyandillegallyburied household waste
525
. The initial data for estimating the volume of the household wastegeneration are: population, coverage of the population by the system of centralized solid wastecollection,specificvolumeofsolidwastegenerationperinhabitant.2. After estimating the volumes of the household waste generation, these volumes are divided intoseparate streams of household waste components, the value of which, in turn, is determinedonthebasis of their component (morphological) composition. These streams are: paper andcardboard,foodwaste andfoodindustrywaste at all stages of productionandconsumption, wastefromgreenspaces,wood, personal hygiene products, rubber and leather, textiles and non-biodegradable components(includingferrous metals, non-ferrous metals, glass, plastic, dangerousandotherinorganicwaste).Atthe same time, householdwaste that is not coveredbythecentralizedcollectionsystemisdisposedofinunmanagedshallowlandfills.3. Foodwaste andfoodindustrywasteatallstagesofproductionandconsumptionandwastefromgreenareas as part of the streamof mixedMSWforma streamfor composting(biological treatment), thevolumeofwhichisdeterminedbythetotalshareofcomposting.
523

Unspecifiedpractices(e.g.homecomposting,grayrecycling,etc.)ofhouseholdwastemanagementnotcoveredbythecentralizedcollectionsystemareexcludedfromthemassbalancebecausetheydonotresultinsignificantGHGemissions.

ContinuationofAppendix4tothePlanIt shouldbe notedthat the issue of increasingRESwaste (includingcomponents of solar panels andwindturbines) andtheir processingmethods for the purposes of modelingGHGemissionsinthe"Waste"sectorwas not considered, because such emissions are insignificant in the context of forecasting emissions byIPCCemissionsources inthe "Waste" sector. The questionof growingbiomass withthe aimofitsfurtheruse for energy purposes was also not considered in the "Waste" sector, because according to the IPCCdefinitions,suchactivityisnotevaluatedinthe"Waste"sector.Adherence to the principle of "Do no significant harm"inthe context of the development of wastethermaltreatmenttechnologiesThe principle "Do No Significant Harm" is the basis for prioritizing the development of this or thattechnologyunder the conditions of sustainable development of the country. It is basedonthe conceptthatthe development of activities thatcauseasignificantnegativeimpactontheenvironmentalgoalsdefinedinArticle17ofEURegulation2020/852cannotbeencouraged.Consideringthat onlymoderntechnologies of thermal treatment of waste cancomplywiththeprincipleof"No significant harm" and taking into account the five-level hierarchy of waste definedinDirective No.2008/98/EC, in whichthermal treatment methods are inthe penultimate place inorder of priority, inboththe WEMandWAMscenarios,wasteheattreatmenttechnologiesfoundlimiteduse.Thus,accordingtotheWEMscenario, the share of heat treatment will reach7%by2030and10%by2050;andundertheWAMscenario–8%by2030and15%by2050. These indicators are significantlylower thanthe correspondingindicators of those European countries that have made significant progress in the transition toa circulareconomy: for example, the share of thermal treatment of solid household waste in Switzerland is about48%, in Belgium- 46%; Sweden – 59%; Denmark - 39%, etc. For more details, see Figure 5.5, whichshowsthemainindicatorsofsolidhouseholdwastemanagementinEuropeancountriesfor2022.Moreover, it is possible that in the long term, with the further development of thermal treatmenttechnologies, the role of these technologies inthe waste management systeminUkrainemayberevisedinthe direction of intensifying their distribution, provided the principle of "Doing no significant harm" isobserved.The target indicators of thermal treatment of solidwaste inUkraineinbothWEMandWAMscenarios,onthe one hand, were agreed with the normative legal documents in the field of waste management inUkraine, andontheotherhand,correspondtotherecommendationsprovidedintheframeworkofanumberof projects of international technical assistance toUkraine onsustainable andlow-carbondevelopment ofthewastemanagementsysteminUkraine,including:● the international technical assistance project "Assessment of technological needs in Ukraine" for thewaste sector, carriedout in2018-2020withinthe frameworkof GEFfundingandimplementedbyUNEnvironmentandUNEPDTUPartnership.● the international technical assistance project "Supportinginvestmentsinthesystemofsustainablesolidwaste management inUkraine", withthe financialsupportoftheMultidonorAccountforUkraine,wasimplementedbytheEuropeanBankforReconstructionandDevelopmentin2017.
